parts.name: OPIc Interview
parts.dir: 질문을 듣고 자유롭게 답합니다. 문항별 제한 시간은 없으며 권장 답변 시간은 1분 30초~2분입니다. 질문은 한 번 다시 들을 수 있습니다. 7번 문항 뒤에 난이도 재조정(쉽게/비슷하게/어렵게) 화면이 나옵니다.

items.q: Let's start the interview now. Tell me a little bit about yourself.

say.t: Let's start the interview now. Tell me a little bit about yourself.

items.model: Hi, nice to meet you. My name is Minjun, and I'm thirty-two years old. Um, I work as an office worker at a mid-sized logistics company, so most of my day is spent in front of a computer, answering e-mails and, you know, preparing reports for my team. These days we're on a hybrid schedule, so I go into the office three days a week and work from home the other two, which I really like. I live with my parents and my younger sister in an apartment in Gunpo. It's pretty close to a big park, so I take a walk there almost every evening after dinner. In my free time, I usually listen to music or hang out at cafés with my friends. Honestly, I'm kind of a homebody, but on long weekends I like to take short trips around Korea with my family. Recently I started studying English again because I want to get a better position at work. So, yeah, that's a little bit about me. Thanks for listening!
items.tip:
자기소개는 채점에 큰 비중은 없지만 첫인상(발음·자신감)을 만든다. 1분 내외로 짧고 자연스럽게.
이름·직업 → 사는 곳·가족 → 여가(서베이에 고른 것) → 요즘 근황 순서. 외운 티 나는 문어체보다 'you know, honestly, so yeah' 같은 구어 연결어를 섞을 것.

items.q: In your background survey, you indicated that you like to go to parks. Tell me about a park you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like? Please describe it in as much detail as possible.

say.t: In your background survey, you indicated that you like to go to parks. Tell me about a park you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like? Please describe it in as much detail as possible.

items.model: Oh, sure. The park I go to most often is a big lake park about ten minutes from my apartment. It's, um, right in the middle of the neighborhood, so lots of people go there. When you walk in, the first thing you see is a huge lake with a wooden walking path around it. The path is about two kilometers long, and there are benches every hundred meters or so, where you can sit and just look at the water. On one side, there's a playground for kids and a small outdoor gym with exercise machines, and on the other side, there's a field full of flowers, which looks amazing in spring. Oh, and there's a little convenience store near the main gate, so you can grab a drink or some snacks. At night, the lights along the path are turned on, and the reflection on the lake is really beautiful. Honestly, it's my favorite place in the whole neighborhood because it's peaceful and green, even though it's in the middle of the city. So, yeah, that's the park I usually go to.
items.tip:
묘사 문제는 '위치 → 첫인상 → 공간을 한 바퀴 돌듯 왼쪽/오른쪽/입구 → 내가 좋아하는 이유' 동선으로 말하면 막히지 않는다.
숫자(10분, 2km, 100m마다)를 넣으면 구체성이 확 올라간다. 마지막에 감정 한 줄로 마무리.

items.q: What do you usually do when you go to the park? Who do you usually go with, and what do you do from the time you arrive until you leave? Tell me about your routine in detail.

say.t: What do you usually do when you go to the park? Who do you usually go with, and what do you do from the time you arrive until you leave? Tell me about your routine in detail.

items.model: Well, I usually go to the park on weekday evenings, right after dinner, around eight o'clock. Most of the time I go alone, but on weekends my dad sometimes comes with me. First, I put on my earphones and pick a playlist, because walking without music is kind of boring for me. Then I do a few stretches near the entrance, just to warm up a little. After that, I walk around the lake two times, which takes about forty minutes. If I'm feeling energetic, I jog for part of the way, but usually I just walk at a fast pace. Um, while I'm walking I don't really think about work, so it's a great way to clear my head. When I finish, I sit on one of the benches for a few minutes and drink some water. Sometimes I stop by the convenience store and buy an ice cream, which I know kind of ruins the exercise, haha. Then I walk back home and take a shower. So that's basically my park routine. It's simple, but it really helps me relax after a long day.
items.tip:
루틴 문제는 시간 순서 연결어(First, Then, After that, When I finish)가 핵심. 현재시제(습관)로 통일할 것.
'누구와·언제·얼마나'를 초반에 깔고, 중간에 감정·유머 한 줄(아이스크림)을 넣으면 IH 느낌이 난다.

items.q: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a park. When was it, who were you with, and what happened? Why was it so memorable?

say.t: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a park. When was it, who were you with, and what happened? Why was it so memorable?

items.model: Oh, I have a really memorable one. It was last spring, I think around April, and I went to the lake park with my younger sister. We planned to have a little picnic, so we packed some sandwiches and fruit and brought a blanket. When we got there, the cherry blossoms were in full bloom, and it was super crowded, but we found a nice spot under a tree. Everything was perfect for, like, thirty minutes. Then suddenly the sky got really dark and it started pouring rain. We didn't have an umbrella, so we grabbed our stuff and ran to a small pavilion near the playground. The funny thing was, about twenty other people had the same idea, so we were all squeezed together under this tiny roof. At first it was awkward, but then an older lady started sharing her snacks with everyone, and people began chatting and laughing. When the rain stopped, there was a rainbow over the lake, and everyone took pictures together. It was memorable because a ruined picnic turned into one of the warmest moments I've ever had with strangers. My sister and I still talk about it.
items.tip:
경험 문제는 '언제·누구와 → 배경 → 사건(갑자기!) → 해결 → 왜 기억에 남는지' 스토리 구조. 과거시제를 끝까지 유지.
'Then suddenly ~', 'The funny thing was ~' 같은 전환 표현으로 반전을 만들면 듣는 사람이 몰입한다.

items.q: You indicated in the survey that you enjoy listening to music. What kinds of music do you like to listen to? Who are some of your favorite singers or musicians, and why do you like them?

say.t: You indicated in the survey that you enjoy listening to music. What kinds of music do you like to listen to? Who are some of your favorite singers or musicians, and why do you like them?

items.model: Um, I like a lot of different kinds of music, but I'd say my favorites are indie pop and acoustic music. I like songs with soft guitar and simple melodies, because they help me calm down, especially after a stressful day at work. When I'm working out or walking fast, though, I switch to something more upbeat, like dance pop or electronic music. As for musicians, one of my favorites is a Korean indie band called Paper Lantern. Their songs are kind of quiet and dreamy, and the lyrics are about everyday life, like riding the bus home or eating alone, so I can really relate to them. I've been listening to them for about five years. I also like a solo singer named Hana Seo, who plays the piano and sings at the same time. Her voice is really warm and a little bit husky, and her live performances are amazing. Honestly, I think I like these musicians because their music feels honest, not too commercial. So, yeah, that's the kind of music I'm into.
items.tip:
'어떤 장르 + 왜 좋은지 + 좋아하는 가수 + 이유' 네 덩어리로 나눠 말한다. 가수 이름은 지어낸 이름이어도 괜찮다 — 중요한 건 설명.
상황에 따라 듣는 음악이 다르다(When I'm ~, though, ~)는 대조를 넣으면 문장 구조가 다양해진다.

items.q: When and where do you usually listen to music? What devices do you use? Tell me about your typical music-listening habits.

say.t: When and where do you usually listen to music? What devices do you use? Tell me about your typical music-listening habits.

items.model: Well, I listen to music pretty much all day, to be honest. In the morning, I listen on my way to the office. It takes about forty minutes by subway, so I put on my wireless earbuds and play a morning playlist on my phone. I usually choose something bright and energetic to wake myself up. At work, I can't really listen to music when I'm in the office, but on my work-from-home days, I play quiet instrumental music through a small Bluetooth speaker while I'm writing reports. It actually helps me focus. In the evening, I listen to music while walking in the park, like I said before. And before I go to bed, I sometimes use the smart speaker in my room and ask it to play something relaxing. I mostly use a music streaming app, and I like that it recommends new songs based on what I listen to. Oh, and on weekends, I sometimes listen to old CDs on my dad's stereo, just for fun. So I guess music is with me from morning till night.
items.tip:
하루 일과(아침 → 일할 때 → 저녁 → 자기 전)를 따라가면 습관 문제를 길게 말할 수 있다.
기기 질문이 있으니 earbuds, Bluetooth speaker, smart speaker, streaming app 같은 단어를 자연스럽게 섞을 것. 앞 문제와 연결('like I said before')하면 일관성 점수에 도움.

items.q: How did you first become interested in music? Tell me about how your taste in music has changed over the years, from when you were younger until now.

say.t: How did you first become interested in music? Tell me about how your taste in music has changed over the years, from when you were younger until now.

items.model: Hmm, I think I first got into music when I was in middle school. My older cousin gave me his old MP3 player, and it was full of rock songs. I listened to them every single day on the way to school, and I even tried to learn the guitar, although I gave up after a few months, haha. Back then, I only liked loud, fast music, because it made me feel kind of cool and rebellious. In high school, I started listening to K-pop with my friends, mainly because everyone was talking about it and I didn't want to be left out. Then in college, my taste changed a lot. I joined a music club, and my friends there introduced me to indie and acoustic music. At first I thought it was boring, but the more I listened, the more I liked it. These days, I mostly listen to calm music, probably because my life is busier and I need something to help me relax. So I'd say my taste has gone from loud to quiet as I've gotten older. It's funny how music kind of follows your life.
items.tip:
시간 흐름(중학생 → 고등학생 → 대학생 → 지금)으로 변화를 보여주는 문제. Back then / In high school / These days 같은 시점 표현을 분명히.
'used to', 'at first ~ but the more ~ the more ~' 구문을 쓰면 IH 이상 문법 범위를 보여줄 수 있다.

items.q: Now I'd like to ask you about recycling. Tell me how people recycle in your country. What kinds of things do they recycle, and how is the recycling system organized?

say.t: Now I'd like to ask you about recycling. Tell me how people recycle in your country. What kinds of things do they recycle, and how is the recycling system organized?

items.model: Oh, recycling. Well, in Korea, recycling is actually pretty strict, and most people take it seriously. If you live in an apartment like me, there's usually a recycling area in the parking lot with lots of big bins. Each bin is for a different type of item, like paper, plastic, glass, cans, and styrofoam. You have to separate everything carefully. For example, if you throw away a plastic bottle, you're supposed to take off the label and wash it first. Food waste is separate, too. In many apartments, you put it in a special machine and pay with a card, depending on how much it weighs. For general trash that can't be recycled, you have to buy official trash bags from the local government, so the more trash you throw away, the more you pay. Oh, and in my apartment, recycling day is only on Wednesdays, so everyone rushes out with their bags that night. Honestly, it can be a little annoying, but I think the system works well and it really reduces waste.
items.tip:
돌발 주제는 준비 없이 나와도 '시스템 개요 → 종류별 분리 → 구체 예시 → 내 의견' 틀로 버틴다.
'be supposed to', 'depending on', 'the more ~ the more ~'처럼 규칙을 설명하는 표현을 미리 익혀 둘 것. 한국식 종량제·음식물 카드 등 디테일이 고득점 포인트.

items.q: What do you personally do to recycle at home? Describe your recycling routine, from sorting the items to taking them out.

say.t: What do you personally do to recycle at home? Describe your recycling routine, from sorting the items to taking them out.

items.model: Okay, so at my house, we have a small recycling corner next to the kitchen. There are four plastic boxes there: one for paper, one for plastic, one for cans and glass, and one for vinyl bags. Whenever we finish something, like a milk carton or a yogurt cup, we rinse it out first and then put it in the right box. My mom is really strict about it, so if I put something in the wrong box, she definitely lets me know, haha. Delivery boxes are the most annoying part, because we order a lot online. I have to remove all the tape and labels and fold the boxes flat. Then, every Wednesday evening, it's my job to take everything down to the recycling area in the parking lot. It usually takes two trips with the elevator. Once I'm there, I sort everything into the big bins, and then I come back and wipe the boxes clean. It takes maybe twenty minutes in total. It's a small thing, but I feel like I'm doing my part for the environment.
items.tip:
루틴은 '장소(어디에 모으나) → 분류 → 세척 → 배출 요일·담당 → 소감' 순서. 현재시제·빈도부사(whenever, every Wednesday)를 꼭.
가족 이야기(엄마가 엄격함)처럼 사람을 넣으면 답변이 생생해지고 길이도 자연스럽게 늘어난다.

items.q: Have you ever had a problem or an unusual experience related to recycling? Tell me what happened, how you dealt with it, and what you learned from it.

say.t: Have you ever had a problem or an unusual experience related to recycling? Tell me what happened, how you dealt with it, and what you learned from it.

items.model: Yes, actually, something kind of embarrassing happened about a year ago. We had just moved into a new apartment, and I didn't know the recycling rules there yet. In our old building, you could throw away recycling any day, so one Sunday I took down a huge pile of boxes and plastic. I left everything neatly next to the bins and went back upstairs. The next morning, there was a notice in the elevator with a photo of my boxes, saying, 'Please follow the recycling schedule!' I was so embarrassed, because my apartment number was written on one of the delivery labels. So I went straight to the management office and apologized. The manager was actually really nice. He explained that recycling day was Wednesday only and gave me a printed guide. Then I went back, picked up all my stuff, and brought it home again, haha. Since then, I always check the rules first whenever I move or visit a new place. I learned that every building has its own system, and it's better to ask than to guess.
items.tip:
문제-해결 경험은 '상황 배경 → 실수/문제 → 결과(공지문!) → 대처 → 교훈' 5단. 과거시제 유지가 가장 중요.
직접 인용('Please follow ~!')을 한 번 넣으면 스토리텔링 점수가 오른다. 교훈 한 문장으로 깔끔하게 끝낼 것.

items.q: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You are planning a weekend trip to a seaside town with your family, and you want to stay at a small guesthouse there. Call the guesthouse and ask three or four questions to find out what you need to know before you book.

say.t: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You are planning a weekend trip to a seaside town with your family, and you want to stay at a small guesthouse there. Call the guesthouse and ask three or four questions to find out what you need to know before you book.

items.model: Hello, is this Bluewave Guesthouse? Hi, my name is Minjun, and I'm planning a family trip to your town next month. I found your guesthouse online and it looks really nice, so I have a few questions before I make a reservation. First, do you have a room available for four people on the weekend of the 14th? We'd be checking in on Saturday and leaving on Sunday. Second, um, is breakfast included in the price, or do we have to pay extra for it? My parents usually like to eat early, so if it's included, what time does it start? Third, how far is the guesthouse from the beach? Is it walking distance, or would we need to drive? And if we drive, is there free parking for guests? Oh, and one more thing. My father has trouble with stairs, so I was wondering if the room is on the first floor or if there's an elevator. Okay, I think that's everything. Could you let me know the price as well? Thank you so much for your help.
items.tip:
롤플레이 11번은 '인사·자기소개 → 전화 목적 → 질문 3~4개 → 마무리 인사'. 질문 앞에 First / Second / And one more thing으로 번호를 붙이면 조직력이 보인다.
의문문 형태를 다양하게(Do you ~? / Is ~? / How far ~? / I was wondering if ~)— 같은 패턴 반복은 감점 요인.

items.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. You have booked the guesthouse, but you just found out that you have to work that weekend because of an urgent project. Call the guesthouse and leave a message explaining the situation, and suggest two or three alternatives to solve the problem.

say.t: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. You have booked the guesthouse, but you just found out that you have to work that weekend because of an urgent project. Call the guesthouse and leave a message explaining the situation, and suggest two or three alternatives to solve the problem.

items.model: Hi, this message is for the owner of Bluewave Guesthouse. My name is Minjun Lee, and I booked a family room for this coming Saturday, the 14th. Um, unfortunately, I have a bit of a problem. I just found out that I have to work this weekend because of an urgent project at my company, so I'm really sorry, but I won't be able to come on that date. I know it's short notice, so I'd like to suggest a few options. First, would it be possible to move our reservation to the following weekend, the 21st? We'd still be four people, and we'd be happy to stay in the same type of room. Second, if that weekend is already full, could we change it to any weekend next month instead? We're pretty flexible. And if neither of those works, could you please cancel the booking and tell me how much of the deposit I can get back? I'll understand if there's a cancellation fee. Please call me back at 010-1234-5678 when you get this. Again, I'm really sorry for the trouble, and thank you for understanding.
items.tip:
13번 직전의 '문제 해결' 롤플레이는 '누구인지 → 문제 상황 → 사과 → 대안 2~3개 → 연락처·마무리' 구조가 정답.
대안은 Would it be possible to ~? / Could we ~ instead? / If neither of those works, ~ 처럼 정중한 제안 표현으로. 메시지 남기기 상황이므로 상대 대답을 기다리지 말고 혼자 끝까지 말한다.

items.q: That's the end of the situation. Have you ever had to change or cancel your plans at the last minute because of something unexpected? Tell me what happened and how you handled the situation.

say.t: That's the end of the situation. Have you ever had to change or cancel your plans at the last minute because of something unexpected? Tell me what happened and how you handled the situation.

items.model: Yeah, that actually happened to me two years ago. My friends and I had planned a trip to Jeju Island for three days during the summer holidays. We booked flights, a rental car, and a nice pension near the beach, and we were so excited. But the day before we were supposed to leave, a big typhoon was heading toward Jeju, and all the flights got canceled. At first, we were really disappointed, and honestly, kind of stressed out, because we had already paid for everything. So we sat down at a café and made a plan. First, I called the airline, and luckily they gave us a full refund because it was a weather issue. Then my friend called the pension, and the owner kindly let us change the dates to the next month without any fee. The rental car was the hardest part, but we got most of our money back in the end. Instead of going to Jeju that weekend, we took a train to Gangneung, which wasn't affected by the storm. It turned out to be a really fun trip. Since then, I always check the weather and the cancellation policy before I book anything.
items.tip:
롤플레이 마지막 문항은 앞 상황과 '관련된 내 실제 경험'. 사건 → 감정 → 해결 과정(First, Then) → 결과 → 교훈.
'It turned out to be ~', 'in the end', 'Since then' 같은 결과·변화 표현으로 마무리하면 완성도가 높아진다.

items.q: You indicated that you like going to cafés. How have cafés in your country changed compared to when you were younger? What are the biggest differences between cafés in the past and cafés today?

say.t: You indicated that you like going to cafés. How have cafés in your country changed compared to when you were younger? What are the biggest differences between cafés in the past and cafés today?

items.model: Hmm, that's an interesting question. Cafés have changed a lot in Korea, I think. When I was a teenager, cafés were mostly just places to meet friends and have a coffee. There weren't that many of them, and coffee was kind of expensive, so we only went there on special occasions. The menu was simple, and most cafés looked pretty similar. These days, though, there's a café on almost every corner, and they're much more diverse. Some cafés are huge, with beautiful interiors designed for taking photos, and people even travel to other cities just to visit them. Others are tiny takeout places where you can grab a cheap coffee in a minute. Another big difference is how people use cafés. Now, lots of people go there to study or work on their laptops for hours, so many cafés have power outlets at every table. And the way we order has changed, too. In the past, you ordered from a person at the counter, but now you often order through a kiosk or an app before you even arrive. Overall, I'd say cafés have become less about coffee and more about space and convenience.
items.tip:
비교 문제는 'In the past ~ → These days, though ~' 대조를 최소 2~3쌍 만든다(개수·인테리어·이용 목적·주문 방식).
'Another big difference is ~', 'Overall, I'd say ~'로 구분과 결론을 분명히. 과거(were, ordered)와 현재(are, order) 시제 대비가 채점 포인트.

items.q: Many cafés and restaurants now use self-order kiosks and mobile apps instead of staff taking orders. What concerns or issues do people have about this change? Why do you think people feel this way, and what could be done about it?

say.t: Many cafés and restaurants now use self-order kiosks and mobile apps instead of staff taking orders. What concerns or issues do people have about this change? Why do you think people feel this way, and what could be done about it?

items.model: Well, I think this is a really important issue these days. On the one hand, kiosks and apps are convenient for young people like me. They're fast, and you can see the whole menu with pictures. But on the other hand, a lot of people are worried about this change. The biggest concern is that older people, or people who aren't comfortable with technology, find kiosks really difficult to use. For example, my grandmother once stood in front of a kiosk for about five minutes and then just left the café without ordering, because the screen was too complicated and the people behind her were waiting. She said she felt embarrassed and kind of left out. Another concern is jobs. Since machines are taking orders, some people worry that part-time workers, especially students, will have fewer job opportunities. I think people feel this way because the change happened very quickly, and not everyone was ready for it. To solve this, I think stores should keep at least one staff member to help customers, and kiosks should have an easy mode with bigger letters and voice guidance. That way, technology can be convenient for everyone, not just some people.
items.tip:
사회 이슈 문제는 '장점 인정(On the one hand) → 우려 1(+구체 사례) → 우려 2 → 원인 분석 → 해결책' 순서. IH/AL을 가르는 문항이라 의견과 근거가 분명해야 한다.
가족·지인 사례를 하나 넣으면 추상적인 답변을 피할 수 있다. 'I think people feel this way because ~', 'That way, ~'로 논리 연결.
